note: Every rule marked scope=fixtures must be covered by at least one case in the corpus. Rules marked scope=elsewhere are real product rules that a rule-evaluator fixture cannot express; each one names where it is enforced instead. The validator checks both halves of this.

rules.text: A restriction is active when its rule is enabled, no bypass is active for that application, and the rule's own condition holds.
Always-on mode: the condition always holds.
Schedule mode: the current weekday is selected and local time falls inside the interval.
Daily limit mode: measured usage of that application today has reached the limit.
An interval such as 22:00-07:00 crosses midnight.
Schedules are stored in local time.
Bypass grants store an absolute expiry.
A daily limit resets at local midnight.
Usage measurement is approximate, so a daily limit triggers slightly late rather than exactly at the limit.
Rule priority: always-on, then schedule, then daily limit.
When several rules apply, the user sees one clear reason while all reasons are preserved in the event record.
After a bypass is granted, the block must not appear again for that application until the grant expires.

rules.enforcedBy: The detection layer, not the rule evaluator. A critical system application never reaches rule evaluation because it is excluded before it. Verified on the emulator in spikes A-01 and A-02, and required again in phase 12.
rules.text: BlockSocial never blocks itself, system settings, the launcher, the phone app, or critical system UI.

rules.enforcedBy: The statistics and presentation layer, phase 18. The corpus does express the measurement side of it: a running session is a lower bound, and daily-limit cases carry an explicit tolerance rather than implying an exact cutoff.
rules.text: Statistics never show false precision. A metric a platform cannot measure is hidden, not shown as zero.
A manual focus session, if it ships later, sits directly below always-on in the priority order. The MVP has nothing in that slot, but the order must already reserve it.
